items.title: Vercel CLI can now set new projects to expire
items.summary: You can now set a new project to expire when you deploy it with . Expired projects are deleted automatically, so prototypes, demos, and test apps don't need cleaning up by hand.Vercel CLIRun  with  and a duration:vercel deploy--delete-project-afterSupported durations are , , , , and , and the CLI prints the date and time when the project expires. The flag only applies when  creates the project. If you deploy to an existing project with the flag, its expiration doesn't change and the CLI prints a warning.1h1d1w2w30dvercel deployTo remove a project's expiration, run :vercel project keepUpdate Vercel CLI to  or later to get started. Learn more in the .v65.12.0vercel deploy documentationRead more

items.title: Vercel Tracing is now generally available
items.summary: is now generally available on all plans. You can now search and inspect traces from the  or the , and new Next.js projects get tracing by default. Pricing is unchanged from the beta.Vercel TracingdashboardVercel CLIIn beta, you could only open a trace per request from the Logs page. The new Traces page shows every trace and span in one place, for a project or your whole team. Switch between a Spans list and a Traces list, filter each, and search with  (KQL). A Live mode streams new traces as they arrive. A query like  narrows to slow database spans by name and duration.Kibana Query Languagespan.name:db* AND span.duration > 500The Traces page uses the same KQL as , so a query built in the dashboard runs in the CLI unchanged. Search covers every project in your team, or one project with the  flag. Inspect a single trace with , and manage a project's sampling rules with .vercel traces search --query--projectvercel traces inspect <request-id>vercel traces configIn beta, nothing was collected until you added a sampling rule. Starting with Next.js 16.5, new projects created on Vercel that include at least one Node.js function get tracing turned on after their first successful build. Vercel adds one sampling rule tracing 100% of requests in all environments and injects instrumentation at build time, so traces include Next.js framework spans with no setup. To opt out, remove all sampling rules in Settings → Tracing.In beta, traces followed your runtime log retention. Hobby now keeps traces for 3 days instead of 1 hour, Pro for 14 days instead of 1 day, and Enterprise for 14 days instead of 3 days.Read the  to learn more.Tracing documentationRead moreBrowse and search traces in the dashboardSearch traces from the CLIAutomatic tracing for new Next.js projectsLonger retention
